object: The interpretation of quantum mechanics developed primarily by Niels Bohr and Werner Heisenberg in the mid-1920s.  Physical systems do not have definite properties prior to measurement; the act of observation collapses the wave function into a definite state.  The interpretation that won at Solvay and dominated physics for most of the twentieth century.
